content:
ACME Support: Hey, streaming is dropping for us mid-request when a mobile user switches from LTE -> WiFi. They get partial output and the client never resumes. Happening for ~5% of sessions since last deploy.

Alex P: Thanks — can you paste the raw chunked stream logs and the client code? Is this EventSource / fetch / websocket?

ACME Support: Using EventSource in a React Native WebView wrapper. We see HTTP 200 then a few SSE messages, then connection disappears. No reconnect attempts from the client side (EventSource 'onerror' fires but no retry).

Maria S: Curious — RN WebView + EventSource is brittle with network handoffs. Two things to check: 1) whether the client re-creates EventSource on error, 2) if there's any intermediary (corporate proxies / mobile carrier NAT) that kills idle TCP after network change. Can we get a tcpdump or server-side socket close reason?

ACME Support: We grabbed server logs. Here's the relevant excerpt (timestamps redacted):

```
[INFO] request_id=abcd1234 client=10.4.5.6 Accept: text/event-stream
[DEBUG] stream_open request_id=abcd1234 handler=stream.handler
data: {"delta":"Hello"}\\n\\n
[DEBUG] client_closed request_id=abcd1234 reason=RST
[WARN] incomplete_stream request_id=abcd1234 last_chunk_id=2
```

Sam K: RST indicates the client TCP connection closed abruptly (likely network). On mobile switching from LTE to WiFi you'll often get a RST or FIN on the old socket. Two follow-ups: 1) does your client set Last-Event-ID when reconnecting? 2) are we including SSE retry hints?

ACME Support: EventSource implementation we use doesn't set Last-Event-ID automatically for partial messages. We also don't currently emit a ``retry: 3000\n`` SSE line.

Alex P: That explains part of it. If EventSource reconnects without Last-Event-ID, server can't resume exactly and client will likely re-request from zero — but here the client didn't reconnect. Could be RN WebView losing network access or JS thread pause.

Jordan (oncall): Quick mitigation options:
- Send heartbeat pings over SSE every 15s (a comment line or zero-length event) so NATs don't idle out. Example: `: ping\n\n` or `data: \n\n` lines.
- Add `retry: 3000` at stream start to tell EventSource to retry.
- Advise client to re-create EventSource on 'error' with exponential backoff and send Last-Event-ID header if available.

Nate - infra: Also check our edge / LB timeouts. If we have `proxy_read_timeout` or HTTP/1.1 keepalive shorter than mobile NAT TTL, we can get abrupt closes. Sharing an nginx snippet we use in other SSE endpoints:

```
proxy_buffering off;
proxy_cache off;
proxy_read_timeout 3600s;
proxy_send_timeout 3600s;
chunked_transfer_encoding on;
```

Sam K: Another gotcha is HTTP/2 middleboxes. If the client flips networks, sometimes we see `HTTP/2 stream reset` at the server. We should log ALPN and see whether connection is h2 or h1. For repro: try reproducing with adb (Android) by toggling wifi with `svc wifi enable/disable` while the EventSource is open. I can paste a small repro script: 

```
# reproduce (Android emulator)
adb shell am start -n com.yourapp/.MainActivity
# open stream in-app
sleep 5
adb shell svc wifi disable
sleep 2
adb shell svc wifi enable
# observe server logs for RST/FIN
```

ACME Support: We can try that. Anything server-side we can change quickly?

Maria S: Yes — short-term: add `retry` and heartbeat events. Long-term: support resume tokens. We can also return a small JSON status event every 10s if no data sent. Example SSE block at open:

```
retry: 3000
: stream-open
```

Alex P: For this customer's SLA we should also add diagnostic headers to the stream response so we can correlate client reconnects: `X-Stream-Id`, `X-Client-IP`, `X-Conn-Proto`. That helps trace NAT-level closes.

ACME Support: We'll enable heartbeat + retry tomorrow. One question: how should the client set Last-Event-ID programmatically?

Sam K: On reconnect, EventSource automatically sets Last-Event-ID if the previous event had `id:` lines. If your events don't include `id:` then you need to implement client-side bookmarking. Best pattern: include an incremental `id` field in each SSE event. Then on the server side, support `Last-Event-ID` header to resume. If that's not possible, use sequence numbers in payload and have a resume endpoint.

Jordan (oncall): Also, log sample tcpdump if you can. Useful filter: `tcpdump -w sse-repro.pcap host <client_ip> and port 443`. Look for `RST` flags or `FIN` following a 0-length window. If you see `RST` from client, it's network/handoff. If `RST` from server, we closed due to timeouts/limit.

ACME Support: We ran a few tests. Two captures attached (they reported): one shows client RST after interface change, one shows server side FIN tied to proxy timeout.

Nate - infra: If you have server FIN due to proxy, check our HAProxy config too — `option http-server-close` will close backend connection early. We should use `option http-keep-alive` for SSE endpoints and bump timeouts.

Maria S: Summary action items:
- (ACME) Add `id:` to events and enable `retry` + heartbeat.
- (Redwood infra) Confirm edge/proxy timeouts and set higher `proxy_read_timeout` for SSE routes.
- (Devex) Send sample client reconnect snippet for RN WebView (re-create EventSource on error + use Last-Event-ID).
- (Oncall) Add stream-level diagnostic headers for correlation.

support-bot: Ticket #54291 linked to this thread. Assigned to @Alex P, @Nate - infra.

Alex P: I'll follow up after ACME deploys heartbeat/retry. If reconnect still fails, we'll schedule a short screen-share to capture adb logs and tcpdump. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

ACME Support: Thanks — will update once we've rolled the fix and run the mobile handoff test.

Sam K: One more note — if client shows partial UTF-8 fragments at disconnect, make sure you flush at event boundaries (don't break JSON across chunks mid-codepoint). That can make client-side parsers throw and not reconnect.

Jordan (oncall): Marking this resolved for now pending repro verification. If it reappears, ping #incidents and we'll escalate to runtime team.

ACME Support: Closing loop — heartbeat+retry fixed 90% of cases, remaining repros look like carrier NAT behavior. We'll request users to upgrade to the new client version with Last-Event-ID support.
